proposals.before: In Qianlong 36 (1771), the Gepusizhai headman Jielangkazi Suonuomu seized the chieftain's stockade at Gepusizhai and murdered Chieftain Celeng Duobudan. Governor-General Altai once again sent Yuanjun to deliver an imperial proclamation.
proposals.after: In Qianlong 36 (1771), the Gepusizhai headman, allied with Langka's son Suonuomu, seized the chieftain's stockade at Gepusizhai and murdered Chieftain Celeng Duobudan. Governor-General Altai once again sent Yuanjun to deliver an imperial proclamation.
proposals.reason: Chinese 革布什咱頭人結郎卡子索諾木 uses 結 as 'ally with' and 郎卡子索諾木 as 'Langka's son Suonuomu'; the idiomatic English fuses 結 into a false personal name Jielangkazi.

proposals.before: In the thirty-sixth year, the Gepusizhai headman Jielangkazi Suonuomu seized the official stockade of Gepusizhai and killed the chieftain Celeng Duobudan. Governor-General Altai again ordered Yuanjun to go and proclaim instructions.
proposals.after: In the thirty-sixth year, the Gepusizhai headman allied with Langka's son Suonuomu, seized the official stockade of Gepusizhai and killed the chieftain Celeng Duobudan. Governor-General Altai again ordered Yuanjun to go and proclaim instructions.
proposals.reason: Same misreading of 結郎卡子索諾木 as a single fused name rather than verb 結 plus kinship phrase 郎卡子索諾木.

proposals.before: As a provincial official attached to the campaign, Chengpei should never have been involved.
proposals.after: As a Board secretary attached to the campaign, Chengpei should never have been involved.
proposals.reason: 曹司 denotes a Six Boards department post, not a provincial office; 'provincial official' mistranslates the office.

proposals.before: Chengpei, as a provincial official accompanying the army, should not have been involved in this affair.
proposals.after: Chengpei, as a Board secretary accompanying the army, should not have been involved in this affair.
proposals.reason: Same 曹司 mistranslation as in the idiomatic field.

proposals.before: The rebels resisted fiercely. Cong directed his troops in an uphill assault, was struck by a musket ball, and died in battle. The entire force was destroyed. Among those who died with him were Company Commanders Zhang Qingshi and Chen Dingguo and twenty-five others.
proposals.after: The rebels resisted fiercely. Cong directed his troops in an uphill assault, was struck by a musket ball, and died in battle. The entire force was destroyed. Among those who died with him were Company Commanders Zhang Qingshi and Chen Dingguo and others, twenty-five in all.
proposals.reason: Chinese 同死者…等二十五人 means twenty-five dead in total including the named officers, not those two plus twenty-five more.

proposals.before: Serving as a battalion commander under Vice General Mingliang in the Jinchuan campaign, he distinguished himself and rose through successive promotions to regimental commander of the Yuexi Garrison.
proposals.after: Serving as a company commander (qianzong) under Vice General Mingliang in the Jinchuan campaign, he distinguished himself and rose through successive promotions to regimental commander of the Yuexi Garrison.
proposals.reason: 千總 is a company-level Qing rank, not a battalion commander.

proposals.before: As a battalion commander he followed Vice General Mingliang in the Jinchuan campaign with merit, and through accumulated promotions reached regimental commander of the Yuexi Garrison.
proposals.after: As a company commander (qianzong) he followed Vice General Mingliang in the Jinchuan campaign with merit, and through accumulated promotions reached regimental commander of the Yuexi Garrison.
proposals.reason: 千總 should not be rendered as battalion commander.

proposals.before: He then served under Chengdu General Te Cheng'e at Jiangka, hunting bandits, besieging the rebel stockade at Benken, burning its watchtowers, and killing many enemies. He was promoted to deputy vice general for distinguished service.
proposals.after: He then served under Chengdu General Te Cheng'e at Jiangka, hunting bandits, besieging the rebel stockade at Benken, burning its watchtowers, and killing many enemies. He was promoted to deputy vice general of the Maogong Brigade.
proposals.reason: 懋功協副將 names the Maogong Brigade post; the gloss drops the unit.

proposals.before: Soon afterward he followed Chengdu General Te Cheng'e in stationing troops at Jiangka, capturing bandits, besieging the rebel stockade of Benken, burning its watchtowers, and killing many rebels. He was promoted to deputy vice general with merit.
proposals.after: Soon afterward he followed Chengdu General Te Cheng'e in stationing troops at Jiangka, capturing bandits, besieging the rebel stockade of Benken, burning its watchtowers, and killing many rebels. He was promoted to deputy vice general of the Maogong Brigade.
proposals.reason: 懋功協 is the brigade designation omitted by with merit.

proposals.before: He took Kayai as well and opened the route to Jiamu.
proposals.after: He took Kayai as well and captured Tongjiamu.
proposals.reason: 取通甲木 most naturally names the place Tongjiamu rather than opened the route to Jiamu.

proposals.before: He again captured Kayai and opened the route to Jiamu.
proposals.after: He again captured Kayai and took Tongjiamu.
proposals.reason: 通甲木 is better read as the place-name Tongjiamu.

proposals.before: He was soon promoted to Regional Commander of Sichuan.
proposals.after: He was soon promoted to Provincial Military Commander of Sichuan.
proposals.reason: 提督 is the provincial military commander (tidu), above 總兵 (regional commander); the English conflates the two offices.

proposals.before: He was soon promoted to Regional Commander of Sichuan.
proposals.after: He was soon promoted to Provincial Military Commander of Sichuan.
proposals.reason: Same 提督/總兵 conflation in the literal rendering as in the idiomatic field.

proposals.before: In Qianlong 38 (1773), he was again appointed Regional Commander of Sichuan.
proposals.after: In Qianlong 38 (1773), he was again appointed Provincial Military Commander of Sichuan.
proposals.reason: 复為四川提督 means restoration as tidu, not as regional commander (總兵).

proposals.before: In the thirty-eighth year, he was again appointed Regional Commander of Sichuan.
proposals.after: In the thirty-eighth year, he was again appointed Provincial Military Commander of Sichuan.
proposals.reason: Literal English repeats the same 提督 mistranslation as the idiomatic field.

proposals.before: He rose through successive promotions to deputy vice general of the Weizhou Brigade.
proposals.after: He rose through successive promotions to assistant commander of the Weizhou Brigade.
proposals.reason: 副將 is one Qing rank; 'deputy vice general' is a redundant calque that obscures the office.

proposals.before: During a blizzard, Tianbi led his men in a stealthy crossing through the ravine, reached Damubazong, and struck Senggesang and Sedakela;
proposals.after: During a blizzard, Tianbi led his men in a stealthy crossing through the ravine, reached Damubazong, and struck Senggesang at Sedakela;
proposals.reason: 色達克拉 is the allied Ekezhi chieftain under siege; making him a co-object of 擊 with rebel Senggesang reverses s0120–s0121.

proposals.before: A great wind and snowstorm came. Tianbi led troops in a secret crossing through the ravine, reached Damubazong, and attacked Senggesang and Sedakela;
proposals.after: A great wind and snowstorm came. Tianbi led troops in a secret crossing through the ravine, reached Damubazong, and attacked Senggesang at Sedakela;
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise treats Sedakela as a co-target despite his being the Qing-protected chieftain.

proposals.before: The emperor wrote back in his own hand: "Your memorial of loyal heart and righteous courage moved me to tears!
proposals.after: The emperor wrote back in his own hand: "Your memorial of loyal heart and righteousness moved me to tears!
proposals.reason: Chinese 忠肝義 lacks 膽; idiomatic invents 'courage' not present in the source phrasing.

proposals.before: The emperor personally wrote an edict saying: "Your memorial of loyal heart and righteous courage moved me to tears as I read it!
proposals.after: The emperor personally wrote an edict saying: "Your memorial of loyal heart and righteousness moved me to tears as I read it!
proposals.reason: Literal likewise supplies 'courage' for incomplete 忠肝義; align with the characters present.

proposals.before: After Jinchuan was pacified, Qitu Gela'ersijia was captured and brought to the emperor at Rehe. At court interrogation he testified fully to Tianbi's fierce fighting at the moment of death. Lian was pardoned and allowed to return, and was appointed Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
proposals.after: After Jinchuan was pacified, Qitu Gela'ersijia was captured and sent to the emperor's traveling palace at Rehe. At court interrogation he testified fully to Tianbi's fierce fighting at the moment of death. Lian was pardoned and allowed to return, and was appointed Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic drops 行在 ('traveling palace'); the literal correctly retains that the captive was sent to the emperor's traveling court at Rehe.

proposals.before: In the twelfth month Fukang'an's army arrived and the siege of Jiayi was lifted. Daji went out to welcome him, but—thinking himself high in merit after receiving a peerage and still recovering from the siege—he was too harried to perform the full ceremony of presenting arms and armor. Fukang'an took offense and impeached Daji for deceit, deep Green Standard Army corruption, and unreliability.
proposals.after: In the twelfth month Fukang'an's army arrived and the siege of Jiayi was lifted. Daji went out to welcome him, but—thinking himself high in merit after receiving a peerage and reward, and still within the besieged city—he was too harried to perform the full ceremony of presenting arms and armor. Fukang'an took offense and impeached Daji for deceit, deep Green Standard Army corruption, and unreliability.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents 'recovering from the siege'; Chinese 又在圍城中 means he was still in the besieged city, and also omits 拜爵賞's reward alongside the peerage.

proposals.before: Yuanjun was wronged by Guilin, provoked into defending himself, yet could not obtain justice;
proposals.after: Yuanjun met adversity at Guilin, was provoked into seeking to clear himself, yet could not obtain justice;
proposals.reason: 戹於桂林 is adversity at the place Guilin, not a personal agent 'Guilin' wronging him.

proposals.before: Yuanjun suffered adversity at the hands of Guilin, was provoked and wished to clear himself, but could not obtain justice;
proposals.after: Yuanjun suffered adversity at Guilin, was provoked and wished to clear himself, but could not obtain justice;
proposals.reason: At the hands of Guilin treats 桂林 as a person; the Chinese locates the adversity at Guilin.

decisions.reason: 革布什咱頭人結郎卡子索諾木 parses as the Gepusizhai headman allying with Langka's son Suonuomu; fusing 結 into the false name Jielangkazi is a real error, and the proposed English is accurate.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 革布什咱頭人結郎卡子索諾木據革布什咱官寨

decisions.reason: Literal likewise misreads 結郎卡子索諾木 as one name; 結 is the verb 'ally with' and 郎卡子索諾木 is Langka's son Suonuomu.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 革布什咱頭人結郎卡子索諾木

decisions.reason: 承霈以曹司從軍 uses 曹司 for a Six Boards departmental post; 'provincial official' is wrong, and 'Board secretary' correctly names the office.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 承霈以曹司從軍，不當與其事

decisions.reason: Literal repeats the 曹司 error; Board secretary is the accurate rendering of that metropolitan departmental post.
同死者…等二十五人 totals twenty-five dead including the named officers; 'and twenty-five others' inflates the count, and the proposed fix matches the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 同死者都司張清士、陳定國等二十五人

decisions.reason: 千總 is the Qing company-level rank qianzong, not a battalion commander; the proposed rank label is correct.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以千總從副將軍明亮徵金川有功

decisions.reason: Literal likewise over-ranks 千總 as battalion commander; company commander (qianzong) is required.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以千總從副將軍明亮徵金川有功

decisions.reason: 擢懋功協副將 names the Maogong Brigade post; replacing that unit with 'for distinguished service' invents merit language and drops the office designation.
Literal 'with merit' likewise invents wording absent from 擢懋功協副將 and omits the Maogong Brigade; the proposed office title is complete.
又克卡丫，取通甲木 pairs two captures; 通甲木 is the place Tongjiamu, not 'opened the route to Jiamu', and the following sentence's 甲木 is a related but separate place name.
Literal likewise should take 通甲木 as the place Tongjiamu under 取, parallel to 克卡丫.
After 遷松潘鎮總兵, 旋擢四川提督 is a promotion to tidu; Regional Commander conflates 提督 with 總兵, and Provincial Military Commander is correct.
Literal likewise mislabels 四川提督 as Regional Commander; Provincial Military Commander is required.
复為四川提督 restores the tidu post, not a regional commander (總兵) appointment.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 三十八年，复為四川提督

decisions.reason: Literal repeats the same 提督/總兵 conflation; Provincial Military Commander is the correct office.
副將 of the Weizhou Brigade is already correctly identified; 'deputy vice general' is this chapter's established calque for 副將, and 'assistant commander' is only a stylistic relabeling.

decisions.after: During a blizzard, Tianbi led his men in a stealthy crossing through the ravine, reached Damubazong, and struck Senggesang to relieve Sedakela;
decisions.reason: 色達克拉 is the Qing-protected Ekezhi chieftain under siege (s0120), not a co-target with rebel Senggesang; the proposal rightly rejects co-attack wording but wrongly turns Sedakela into a place.

decisions.after: A great wind and snowstorm came. Tianbi led troops in a secret crossing through the ravine, reached Damubazong, and attacked Senggesang to relieve Sedakela;
decisions.reason: Literal likewise must not treat Sedakela as an attack co-object or as a place-name; the action is striking Senggesang to relieve the besieged chieftain.
Other Qingshi gao witnesses read the full idiom 忠肝義膽; the chapter line's truncated 忠肝義 is corrupt, and 'righteous courage' correctly renders that standard phrase rather than inventing wording.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 所奏忠肝义胆，披览为之堕泪

decisions.reason: Same as the idiomatic line: external editions preserve 忠肝義膽, so stripping 'courage' to match the incomplete chapter string is not a supported repair.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 所奏忠肝义胆，披览为之堕泪

decisions.reason: 傳送熱河行在 specifies the emperor's traveling palace at Rehe; idiomatic 'brought to the emperor at Rehe' drops 行在, and the proposed wording restores it.
拜爵賞 is peerage and reward, and 又在圍城中 means still inside the besieged city; 'recovering from the siege' invents a recovery state and omits the reward.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 自以功高拜爵賞，又在圍城中

decisions.reason: In the lunzan, 戹於桂林 parallels 見嫉於溫福 and 為福康安所不容: 桂林 is Governor-General Guilin the person, not a place; 'wronged by Guilin' is accurate.
Literal 'at the hands of Guilin' correctly treats 桂林 as the personal agent of Yuanjun's adversity, matching the commentary's parallel personal constructions with Wenfu and Fukang'an.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 元俊戹於桂林，激而欲自白，不得直

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted repair restores 郎卡子索諾木 as Langka's son Suonuomu; the extracted English label had fused the kinship phrase into 'son of Langka Suonuomu'.
